section_summary.extract_value: This Introduction describes the development and validation history of the Body Appreciation Scale (BAS) and its revision (BAS-2), and states that the present study aims to examine the psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Brazilian adolescents. The authors hypothesize a one-factor structure invariant across gender and weight status, good internal consistency and two-week temporal stability, and expected correlations of BAS-2 with life satisfaction (positive) and with social physique anxiety and BMI (negative).
section_summary.evidence_source: As a contribution to the body image literature, the aim of this study was to examine the psychometric properties of the BAS-2 in Brazilian adolescents. It was also expected that the one-factor structure would be invariant across gender and weight status. Furthermore, it was hypothesized that the instrument would show a good level of internal consistency and temporal stability over a two-week period. In order to provide evidence of construct validity, body appreciation was expected to be positively correlated with life satisfaction and negatively correlated with social physique anxiety and BMI.
